claim: NEXLOAD overwrites 0x5B00-0x5BFF before the game starts, so a snapshot that keeps code, stack or data there starts wrong unless the build restores the whole 256 bytes.
limit: A read of 5B5C alone did not matter in Atom Ant or Ruff and Reddy (real loader showed 0x10 there in every mode); check what the game does with the byte.

evidence.text: Restore the entire 256-byte NEXLOAD printer buffer, not only the start-up tail; 5B00-5BFF workspace restored completely.
Code lives at 5B00-5BEE (entry 5B00); NEXLOAD writes that buffer, so a set-up call in the stub bank copies 5B00-5BFF back.
Stack at 0x5B76, inside the buffer NEXLOAD overwrites, returning into ROM paging code at 0x5BB0; found by scanning builds with nexload=True.
NEXLOAD overwrites the printer buffer before entry; 5B00..5CFF restored.
Game reads 5B5C (its 7FFD copy); setup restores the buffer because keep_printer_buffer was 48K only.
Game reads 0x5B00 before writing it; NEXLOAD overwrote it, so the snapshot's buffer is put back.
